resources.string: Blood pressure, glucose, cholesterol: follow how they change with your treatment.
Based on the latest reading of each marker.
GLP-1 treatment often improves blood pressure, blood glucose and blood lipids.

GLP-1 treatment, and the weight loss that comes with it, often improves blood pressure, blood glucose, HbA1c and blood lipids (LDL cholesterol, triglycerides). Logging your readings and lab results shows the progress the scale doesn\'t, and makes it easy to review with your doctor.
On the charts, the dashed line is the upper limit of the normal range.
No readings yet. Pick what you want to log:
First reading. Add more to follow the trend.
Reference (AHA): normal < 120/80 · elevated 120–129/< 80 · stage 1 130–139 or 80–89 · stage 2 ≥ 140 or ≥ 90 · low < 90/60. Hypertension Canada considers home readings of 135/85 or more high.
Usual resting range for adults: 50–100 bpm. GLP-1 medications can raise it by a few beats per minute; mention a lasting increase to your doctor.
Fasting: 4.0–6.0 mmol/L normal · 6.1–6.9 elevated · ≥ 7.0 high · < 4.0 low. Values after a meal are naturally higher.
< 5.7 % normal · 5.7–6.4 % prediabetes range · ≥ 6.5 % diabetes range. With diabetes, the usual target is 7.0 % or less (Diabetes Canada).
General target: < 3.5 mmol/L. With diabetes or heart disease, the target is often lower (about 2.0 mmol/L or less). Ask your doctor.
Very high reading. Rest 5 minutes and measure again. If it stays above 180/120, contact a health professional right away; call 911 if you have chest pain, shortness of breath or other symptoms.
Below 4.0 mmol/L is low (hypoglycemia). Follow the plan from your care team, especially if you also take insulin or a sulfonylurea.
The diastolic (lower number) must be below the systolic.
Seated, after 5 minutes of rest, arm supported at heart level. Two readings a minute apart give a better picture.
At rest, ideally in the morning before getting up.
Use a fasting value (8 hours without food) to compare with the ranges.
Copy the value from your lab report, in the unit shown.
e.g. fasting, left arm, after coffee

Reference ranges are general values for adults (Hypertension Canada, American Heart Association, Diabetes Canada, Canadian Cardiovascular Society). Your personal targets are set with your doctor. This screen is a logbook, not a diagnosis.
